result:
I made the four changes to the Remap component in `Remap.cs`, and `dotnet build` succeeds with 0 errors and 2 warnings. I didn't open the component in Grasshopper or test its behaviour.

- **Rename:** The input "Value" is now "Number", with nickname "N".
- **Clamp:** There is a new boolean input "Clamp" (nickname "C", default false) at index 5. When true, the result is limited to the target range. This also works when Target Min is greater than Target Max.
- **Normalized:** There is a new second output "Normalized" (nickname "Nrm"). It is the input's position in the source range, and it is not clamped. If Source Min equals Source Max, it comes out as 0, as the old code already did.
- **Subcategory:** Remap moved from "Math" to "Mapping". The "Add" component is still in "Math".

I put Clamp last so the existing input indices don't shift, so existing wires should still connect to the same inputs. I didn't read the 2 warnings.

Nothing else in the project had a boolean input to copy, so Clamp follows the same pattern as the number inputs in `AddComponent.cs`.
